families.mechanism_summary: In a replay-trained DreamerV3 agent, freeze-bracket experiments localize continual failure to the actor while world-model, reward, value and termination heads retain old-task signals. families.state_and_flow: Replay buffer protects predictive and value state; world model owns imagined transitions; grader owns trajectory selection; actor owns executable policy. Imagined transitions never become observed facts, and the actor must be revalidated against the environment.

families.prior_baseline: Experience replay reasonably assumes that replaying old observations and targets will protect the whole agent because all components continue seeing old-task data.
families.tradeoffs_and_coexistence: Dream rehearsal can recover an actor without keeping all real episodes, but adds a world-model error channel, grader selection bias and cost that grows with prior tasks. Real-episode cloning remains cheaper and more grounded when privacy/storage permits.

families.title: HijackKV: New Threat in Position-Independent KV Cache Reuse
families.revision_relation: v1 / first-public owner; later revisions excluded from event-time claims
families.evolution_relation: Direct Evolution: text/position cache hit -> causal-context provenance check -> tenant-scoped reuse or verified recomputation
families.artifact_locator: https://github.com/YichiCS/KV-Cache-Hijack/commit/f9a5c07bddeae9ef4e04582f4ab114f26c9cbec3; https://zenodo.org/records/20403786 (10.5281/zenodo.20403786, md5:7691c6ebaf4a43f18037af8f0adaf93a) — both pre-cutoff; Repository and Zenodo archive predate the cutoff; this proves artifact provenance, not production incidence or universal exploitability.
families.mechanism_summary: An unprivileged attacker prefixes a common benign chunk with optimized adversarial tokens, causing the chunk KV to encode attacker context. A position-independent multi-tenant cache later matches only benign chunk tokens and reuses the contaminated state for a victim. Text sanitizers cannot see the absent prefix; partial recomputation reduces but does not close this channel.
families.state_and_flow: Cache producer context and tenant own provenance; cache index owns matching; scheduler/loader may expose state only after causal-context and trust compatibility checks. Token equality, RoPE repair, tensor shape and checksum do not establish semantic authority.
families.benchmark_contract: Four QA datasets, 200 samples each; Llama/Qwen/Mistral families from 1B to 70B; CacheBlend, EPIC, random, vanilla/full recomputation; AMD EPYC 9334 and four RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs. Default cache ratio 0.3, recomputation 0.1, chunk 32; results include white-/black-box transfer, 0.1-0.5 cache/recompute sweeps and 0-2048 filler tokens. Precision, serving concurrency and production SLO are Not Disclosed.
families.claim_boundary: Supports a vulnerability in the authors’ position-independent multi-tenant reuse model and disclosed implementations. It does not prove ordinary exact-prefix cache reuse is vulnerable in the same way, deployed incidence, cache availability/probing in every platform, or that reported ASR generalizes beyond tested models/data.
families.prior_baseline: Exact-prefix reuse is restrictive but safe-by-construction with respect to preceding causal context; position-independent reuse reasonably relaxes this to improve hit rate when state mismatch is treated only as a quality problem.
families.tradeoffs_and_coexistence: Strict context/tenant binding sacrifices cross-context hit rate; selective recomputation retains more reuse but leaves residual attack surface and compute cost. Cryptographic integrity only proves bytes were not changed—it cannot prove the producer context was authorized.
families.books_review: Ch50 already explains semantic incompatibility of position-independent KV; Ch72 should own the adversarial trust extension: cache provenance and causal context become authorization inputs, not only correctness metadata.
families.integration_section: 跨请求 KV reuse 一旦放松 exact-prefix 条件，cache identity 就同时成为安全边界。攻击者可以让相同 benign chunk 的 KV 携带未出现在 victim input 中的 hostile causal prefix；token match、位置修复、checksum 与 text sanitizer 都不足以证明该 state 可被另一租户消费。安全复用必须绑定 producer tenant/trust domain、可见 causal context、model/adapter/kernel identity 与 recomputation policy；无法证明兼容时回退 exact-prefix 或 full recompute。

artifact_event_time_receipt.boundary: Repository and Zenodo archive predate the cutoff; this proves artifact provenance, not production incidence or universal exploitability.

families.mechanism_summary: Transformer V-O and MLP boundaries admit paired orthogonal changes of basis that preserve full-precision output. GaugeQuant learns skew-symmetric parameters through a Cayley transform, using a stop-gradient LogSumExp proxy for activation L-infinity; base weights receive only the LM gradient, while rotations receive the quantization-basis objective. MLP rotations are block diagonal and remain runtime operations.
families.state_and_flow: Training run owns gauge parameters and auxiliary optimizer state; LM weights preserve their base objective; export owns paired fusion/runtime transforms and quantization semantics; inference validation owns actual kernel/quality gains.
families.benchmark_contract: Qwen2.5-0.5B full fine-tuning and Llama-2-7B LoRA, C4 for 8,192 steps, batch 1, sequence 512 (~4M tokens), WikiText-2 length 2,048; W4A16, W4A4 group-128 and per-token fake quantization. families.prior_baseline: Post-training calibration or fixed/random rotations are reasonable because they leave base training untouched and simplify artifact creation.
families.tradeoffs_and_coexistence: Online basis learning adapts to evolving activations but adds training state, Cayley/block computation, export identity and runtime MLP rotation. PTQ remains cheaper when calibration is representative or kernels cannot consume the learned layout.
